doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

title: Choosing a music scholarship at the University of Kansas
summary: Poston, undecided at 18, took a music scholarship and the education track instead of following baseball.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you have any idea when you were 18 or 19 that you would end up being a hub?

No. No, at that point, just getting out of high school I chose a music scholarship to go to the University of Kansas, so I knew I wanted to do something related to music but I wasn’t exactly sure even going into school what it would be. And of course the choices were music performance or music education. And I really didn’t have any designs on being a professional trumpet player, so I went into the education program. But again, really, coming out of school it was almost a last minute decision to take the music scholarship. I also played baseball and if you would have told me anytime up until about three or four months before I was out of high school that I would have done anything other than follow baseball I would have laughed. I would have thought that was
ridiculous. But something happened where I decided that I really wanted to pursue the music side of things and so I went with the music scholarship at Kansas.
